entry.title: Social Summary: November 22, 2026
entry.summary:
AI-assisted mathematics dominated the day's discussion. Anthropic's Levent Alpöge reportedly produced a proof Claude-assisted Riemann Hypothesis proof formally verified in Lean. A companion claim of a Navier-Stokes finite-time blowup proof with Tristan Buckmaster amplified the excitement, with most posters adding peer-review caveats.

  • Nathan Lambert released a post-training open-problems roadmap; Harrison Chase shared first-party detail on LangChain's production agent learning loops
  • Open-source sentiment ran positive: Clement Delangue celebrated a US House report, and Sebastian Raschka credited US–Chinese open-weight competition for mutual gains
  • Thinking Machines' open-weights Inkling 2 Mini drew technical interest for its small recurrent architecture

entry.title: SITUATION DETECTED: The Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative have formally certified Anthropic mathematic...
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit discussion, Reports that the Lean FRO and Mathlib Initiative have formally certified an AI-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis by Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpoge working with Claude, and congratulated him.

entry.title: SITUATION EXPLAINED: Two mathematicians say they've shown the Navier-Stokes equations can blow up wi...
entry.summary: Building on yesterday's Reddit discussion, Explainer of a claimed 79-page proof by Anthropic's Alpöge and NYU's Tristan Buckmaster showing 3D Navier-Stokes finite-time blowup from smooth initial conditions alone, without external force — a harder formulation than OpenAI's September result. The authors report using Claude and Codex throughout and include a Lean 4 formalization; it was posted the same day Alpöge claimed a Riemann hypothesis proof.

entry.title: Either you believe the AI buildout is over, that AI was a flash in the pan, and that the need for co...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet makes a detailed bull case for the AI buildout: GPU spot prices keep rising, HBM/DRAM is sold out through 2029, frontier training compute doubles roughly every five months, capabilities scale twice as fast as pre-reasoning, inference runs at 70-85% margins, and demand grows geometrically, framing current conditions as a rare buying opportunity.

entry.title: I believe there is a vast, extremely diverse space of possible approaches to learning (for both time...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet argues that the space of possible learning approaches is vast and diverse, and that the current stack of Transformers plus gradient descent and token-space chain-of-thought reasoning is not even in the top 50% for efficiency; he predicts future AI will look nothing like today's technology.

entry.title: all our agents at langchain (internal GTM & content agents, LangSmith Engine) have a learning lo...
entry.summary: Harrison Chase explains that all agents at LangChain, including internal GTM and content agents and LangSmith Engine, share a learning loop with similar components, and links his new writeup on what makes up a knowledge factory.

entry.title: One of the really interesting things about Neon is it seems pretty much no-one at @GoogleDeepMind kn...
entry.summary: The author observes that almost no one at Google DeepMind seemed to realize how good Gemini 4 Neon was at launch, since they described it as merely approaching frontier models; he uses this to argue that internal evals are a very imperfect measure of model utility.

entry.title: New slide deck on the biggest open problems in post-training and how the field got to where it is to...
entry.summary: Nathan Lambert releases a slide deck on major open problems in post-training, framing it as Trillium Labs goals: harness/context design, character training, open-source RL environments, reasoning efficiency, RL scaling laws, multi-agent scaling, and ends with a debate on how RSI is changing research.

entry.title: Levent Alpöge's Claude-assisted Riemann Hypothesis proof has been officially Lean verified.
entry.summary: Tunguz reports that Levent Alpöge's Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis has been officially verified in the Lean proof assistant, a major claim at the intersection of AI and mathematics.

entry.title: American researchers, startups, nonprofits, government, students and hobbyists overwhelmingly benefi...
entry.summary: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue celebrates a new US House report recognizing that Americans broadly benefit from open-source AI regardless of origin, arguing the best response to Chinese open-source AI is to build more American open-source AI rather than ban it, and thanks the report's congressional sponsors.

entry.title: I seriously think US open-weight models wouldn't be this good without Chinese open-weight models and...
entry.summary: Sebastian Raschka argues that US and Chinese open-weight models have mutually driven each other's quality, and that proprietary models benefit from open-weight competition on both capability and price, concluding competition is good.

entry.title: Is it true? It isn't impossible, just impossibly hard Mathematics for humans! Here's the claim: http...
entry.summary: Kirk Borne flags the claim that an Anthropic mathematician has proven the Riemann Hypothesis, quoting coverage describing it as an AI-generated solution to the 167-year-old problem that would cap AI's year-long conquest of mathematics, and invites scrutiny of the claim.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 21, 2026
entry.summary:
AI-assisted mathematics was the day's dominant story: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claimed a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, while Artificial Analysis framed the Millennium Prize Problems as a human-vs-AI scoreboard. Timnit Gebru drew strong engagement criticizing the rushed release over careful 900-page vetting, sustaining healthy skepticism about verification.

  • Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini dominated open-source discussion: Clement Delangue announced the Apache 2.0 release, Artificial Analysis benchmarked the 26B looped MoE, and Soumith Chintala confirmed it runs on 32GB machines
  • OpenAI published original research on combating distillation; Ethan Mollick hypothesized that restricted distillation explains the open-weights slowdown
  • AI-for-science momentum: Demis Hassabis announced an Isomorphic Labs–Merck cancer drug collaboration, and OpenAI shipped MedChemBench plus neurodegenerative disease work
  • Hugging Face's Thom Wolf revealed a proprietary CDN handling exabyte-scale model downloads
  • Google recapped Gemini 4 Neon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen; Greg Brockman showcased GPT-6.2 Astra robotics capability

Overall sentiment blended excitement over AI-for-science breakthroughs and open-source releases with caution about unverified math claims and tightening model security.

At the time, frontier AI models have zero fluid intelligence. They scor...
entry.summary: Francois Chollet reflects on how far AI progressed since mid-2024: models with near-zero fluid intelligence on ARC evolved into reasoning models that saturated ARC 1 through 3, AI writes most code, models tackle Millennium Prize problems, and lab valuations multiplied enormously, alongside massive changes for Nvidia. A retrospective on the paradigm shift to test-time reasoning.

entry.title:
Distillation can reproduce powerful AI capabilities without the safeguards built around them.
We’re...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces new research on combating distillation of its models, examining how capabilities transfer through distillation and how the company detects and disrupts coordinated attempts to extract model capabilities while bypassing built-in safeguards. The findings are intended to strengthen OpenAI's own defenses and support safeguard efforts across the industry.

entry.title:
Millennium Prize Problems: humans and two labs tied with a score of one
➤ Human: Grigori Perelman p...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis frames the Millennium Prize Problems as a scoreboard: Perelman's recognized Poincaré proof for humanity, OpenAI's claimed September solution to Navier-Stokes using an unreleased internal model, and Anthropic's Levent Alpöge posting a claimed Riemann Hypothesis proof developed with Claude. Notes that P vs NP and several other problems remain open and both AI claims await independent verification.

entry.title:
AI downloads broke the usual CDN model
Since this summer, we're running our own CDN at Hugging Face...
entry.summary: Hugging Face CTO/CO-founder Thom Wolf explains why AI downloads broke traditional CDN design: Hugging Face now runs its own CDN shipping nearly 1 exabyte per month (~420 GB/s across 80,000 req/s), serving few enormous files to machines (GPU clusters) rather than many small files to humans. He details how caching assumptions change for massive objects and release-day traffic floods.

@thinkymachines is releasing Inkling 2 Mini as apache 2....
entry.summary: Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue announces that Thinking Machines is releasing Inkling 2 Mini under an Apache 2.0 license, claiming it reaches the Pareto frontier for open agent models, framing it as evidence that American open-source AI remains vibrant.

entry.title: Thinking Machines has released Inkling 2 Mini at 20 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, a...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces Thinking Machines' release of Inkling 2 Mini, a 26B-total/5.4B-active parameter open-weights looped mixture-of-experts transformer scoring 20 on the Intelligence Index, running on a MacBook or DGX Spark, under Apache 2.0 with 1M token context and text/image input.

entry.title: mini model is out. 27B looping MoE, 3B active. fits on a 32GB memory machine. Been running this on m...
entry.summary: Soumith Chintala announces a new small model: a 27B looping MoE with 3B active parameters that fits on a 32GB machine. He reports benchmarking it on DGX Spark and Mac Mini at roughly 75 tok/s decode, notes evals are roughly on par with Qwen 3.8 27B (an existing model released in August), and suggests the local-llama community will be pleased.

entry.summary: MTS Live reports that Anthropic mathematician Alpoge posted a 4-page note claiming a proof of the Riemann hypothesis working with Claude, formalized as ~250,000 pages of Lean code across 14 machine-checkable files, independently checked by MIT's Andrew Sutherland; a separate 940-page human-only GRH draft by Alessandro Masullo surfaced the same day.

entry.title: NEW: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge says he and Claude have solved the Riemann Hypothesis, a ...

entry.title: Social Summary: November 20, 2026
entry.summary:
The community's attention split between Anthropic's historic IPO and the OpenAI vs. Google rivalry. Jeremy Howard declared a turning point, pairing lavish praise for Gemini 4 Neon with a public rollback of GPT-6.2 in his own product.

  • Google's Gemini 4 Neon (GA 2026-11-18) earned strong practitioner validation from Jeremy Howard, though he criticized Antigravity as needing work
  • Sebastian Raschka delivered the deepest technical analysis, dissecting the Marin Mochi 535B-A23B open checkpoint's architecture choices
  • Perplexity drew attention twice: research on self-improving agent skills with production A/B metrics, and Multiagent usage doubling in a day

My co-founders and I starte...
entry.summary: Continuing our coverage from yesterday, Anthropic publishes CEO Dario Amodei's remarks on the company's initial public offering. He recounts his personal history, including losing his father to a later-curable disease, and argues that scientific advances spring from intelligence, positioning AI as a tool to accelerate disease research and treatments for the benefit of humankind.

entry.title:
Whoa, great and even excessive Marin Mochi (535B-A23B) checkpoint drop (in a good way!)
Comes with ...
entry.summary: Sebastian Raschka analyzes the Marin Mochi (535B total, ~23B active) checkpoint release, highlighting a detailed tech report on component choices for training stability and GPU throughput: latent MoE with an extra RMSNorm, 3:1 sliding-window/global gated GQA with partial RoPE and NoPE, short convolutions on keys/attention/MoE outputs, and a novel Exclusive Self-Attention (XSA) mechanism.

entry.title: Sharing new research on self-improving skills in Perplexity Computer. Brain, which already maintains...
entry.summary: Perplexity's CEO shares research on self-improving agent skills in Perplexity Computer: an improvement agent reads full session trajectories (tool calls, reasoning, results), detects recurring patterns, and proposes new or updated skills only with sufficient evidence, with paired replay on failure scenarios and engineer review for built-in skills. An 8-week production randomized test showed 72.9% of users received at least one personal skill vs 6.5% manual, with tool call failures down 11% and dissatisfied threads down 7.6% at no cost or latency penalty.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 19, 2026
entry.summary:
A tense undercurrent ran through both: who controls frontier AI, and is it safe?

  • Demis Hassabis, Logan Kilpatrick, and Google DeepMind announced Neon as a frontier tier between Carbon and Hydrogen
  • Artificial Analysis independently ranked Neon #3 on its Intelligence Index (61) with strong cost-per-task coding results; François Chollet called its price-performance impressive
  • Anthropic's IPO drew an unprecedented safety backlash: the Center for AI Safety and EleutherAI co-founder Thom Wolf publicly signed a letter calling the lab unsafe
  • OpenAI disclosed exponential growth in researchers' AI use and recursive self-improvement indicators, plus up to 14% PPA chip-design gains with AMD in under five months
  • Expert commentary pushed back on hype: Sebastian Raschka likened benchmark comparisons to IQ tests for hiring; Chollet argued latent token demand is effectively infinite, constrained only by cost

Overall sentiment: excitement about Neon's price-performance and AI-accelerated silicon, deep division over Anthropic's accumulating power, and rising focus on AI improving AI itself.

OpenAI argues AI labs should be required to track and publicly report indicators of recursive self-improvement.

entry.title: Introducing Gemini 4 Neon! Pushing the frontier across domains and punching above its model class in...

Massive engagement (~840K views, 11.4K likes).

entry.title:
Gemini 4 Neon is rolling out now.
Sitting between Carbon and Hydrogen, it brings frontier intellige...
entry.summary: Google DeepMind announces the rollout of Gemini 4 Neon, a new frontier model positioned between Gemini 4 Carbon and Hydrogen, targeting fast task completion for complex software engineering, knowledge work, and science.

entry.title: With Antigravity CLI, Neon (xhigh) scores 59 on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, 3 points...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis reports that Gemini 4 Neon (xhigh) running in Antigravity CLI scores 59 on their Coding Agent Index, three points ahead of Gemini 4 Carbon (high) and roughly in line with Claude Code using Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Opus 5.5, while costing significantly less per task ($6.86 vs $12.61-$15.47). Available to Pro and Ultra subscribers.

We adapted Qwen's model specifically for the pi coding agent u...

entry.title: This by Anthropic seems both right & a condemnation of many “agentic solutions” & harnesses being bu...
entry.summary: Ethan Mollick endorses an Anthropic finding that a single general agent often produces better and cheaper results than sprawling multi-subagent harnesses built by separate teams, framing it as a critique of much current agentic architecture.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 17, 2026

AI safety governance dominated the day.   • Clement Delangue framed the Hugging Face–OpenRouter integration as proof open-source wins through collaboration, not zero-sum competition

Outputs (algorithms, models, evaluations) will be released openly, backed by more than 10,000 GPUs and tested in Perplexity products, with regular publications and active hiring across four cities.

entry.title: Claude writes better code when it can verify its work. Checks that used to be expensive, like tests,...

entry.title: AI is a civilizational technology! There are tremendous opportunities and responsibilities for all o...

entry.title: It's great that OpenAI is doing these assessments but they fall short of Sam's commitment to employe...
entry.summary: Neel Nanda critiques OpenAI's external safety assessment pilot by Apollo Research: while welcoming the assessments, he notes they fall short of Sam Altman's employee-like access commitment. Per Apollo, limitations include no Slack access, OpenAI-selected interviewees, logged formal conversations, and access limited to training-run information rather than internal incidents. He argues good access is essential for trust and that OpenAI should present a plan for deeper access.

entry.title: We’re working with @ApolloResearch, @METR_Evals, @TransluceAI, and @GoodfireAI on embedded assessmen...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces an embedded assessments program in partnership with four external AI safety and evaluation organizations: Apollo Research, METR, Transluce, and Goodfire. The initiative gives outside experts deep access to OpenAI's internal models and systems to independently investigate alignment and stress-test the company's safety safeguards, building on its existing internal alignment and risk-management research.
